standard.title: Aluminium and Aluminium Alloy Foil for Pharmaceutical Packaging — Specification
standard.sector: Metallurgical Engineering / Light Metals and their Alloys

sectional_committee.name: Light Metals and Their Alloys Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies the requirements for bare, coated, or laminated aluminium and aluminium alloy foils utilized in pharmaceutical packaging applications. It is strictly applicable to nominal foil thicknesses ranging from 0.020 mm (20 µm) to 0.040 mm (40 µm).
standard.scope: This standard specifies the requirements for bare, coated, or laminated aluminium and aluminium alloy foils utilized in pharmaceutical packaging applications. It is strictly applicable to nominal foil thicknesses ranging from 0.020 mm (20 µm) to 0.040 mm (40 µm).

certification.description: Voluntary / Statutory. While individual pharmaceutical buyers and manufacturing tenders mandate strict conformity to IS 16011 to pass drug-regulatory GMP audits, manufacturers conforming to this standard are authorized to apply to the Bureau of Indian Standards for a certification licence to carry the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) on foil packaging. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to alloy packaging foils.
requirements: Each package of bare or converted aluminium foil may be marked with the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) for certification and identity.
The specification strictly covers three nominal dimensions: 0.020 mm (20 µm), 0.025 mm (25 µm), 0.030 mm (30 µm), and 0.040 mm (40 µm).
Unless otherwise agreed upon between the manufacturer and the purchaser, bare pharmaceutical strip pack foil must be supplied in a fully annealed condition.

Unless otherwise specified, coated blister pack foil must be supplied as as-rolled foil (without receiving a final anneal). It must be coated on one side with heat-seal lacquer, while the other side is coated with shellac or printed.
Unless otherwise specified, pharmaceutical laminates must be supplied with one side of fully annealed foil laminated with 35 gsm LDPE, and the opposite side coated with protective shellac or printed.

a) Coated blister pack foil must have one bright surface and one matte surface; b) Pharmaceutical laminates may have one bright and one matte surface, or both surfaces bright, as specified by the purchaser.

This test is applicable to coated blister pack foils and pharmaceutical laminates. The sealing strength must comply with the minimum limits of Table 6 (minimum 500 g/25 mm across all nominal thicknesses from 20 to 40 µm).
Peel strength testing is strictly applicable to pharmaceutical laminates. It must satisfy the minimum limits of Table 5 (minimum 250 g/25 mm for nominal thicknesses of 30 µm and 40 µm bare foil).
A lot is defined as all foils in a single consignment of the identical width, thickness, and surface finish, manufactured by a single firm under essentially identical production conditions.

Random samples must be drawn separately from each lot for testing: a) Up to 15 rolls: 5 rolls selected (permissible defectives = 0); b) 16 to 25 rolls: 8 selected (permissible defectives = 1); c) 26 to 50 rolls: 13 selected (permissible defectives = 1); d) 51 to 100 rolls: 20 selected (permissible defectives = 2); e) 101 to 300 rolls: 32 selected (permissible defectives = 3); f) More than 300 rolls: 50 selected (permissible defectives = 3).

All sample rolls must be individually evaluated for manufacturing defects, surface defects, and dimensional tolerances. If the cumulative number of defectives is less than or equal to the permissible limit in Table 7, the lot is accepted.
Each finished foil package must be marked with the manufacturer's name, material grade, metallurgical condition (fully annealed or as-rolled), batch number, and date of manufacture.
